pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why must the tin of charcoal stay closed until it is cold? (1 mark)
   A. The charcoal will become white
   B. The tin will float
   C. The charcoal will taste bad
   D. Fresh air can make hot charcoal catch fire

2. Which is the beater of a drum? (1 mark)
   A. The rope
   B. The skin
   C. The shell
   D. The stick or hand that strikes it

3. If you tighten the skin of a drum, the sound becomes (1 mark)
   A. higher
   B. silent
   C. softer for ever
   D. lower

4. Which players are allowed to shoot at goal? (1 mark)
   A. GK and GD
   B. GS and GA
   C. Only C
   D. WA and WD

5. What do you add to a colour to make it lighter? (1 mark)
   A. Black
   B. More of the same colour only
   C. White
   D. Soil

6. Yellow mixed with blue makes (1 mark)
   A. pink
   B. green
   C. purple
   D. orange

7. On the colour wheel, green sits between (1 mark)
   A. yellow and blue
   B. red and yellow
   C. orange and purple
   D. red and blue

8. The steady pulse in a piece of music is called the (1 mark)
   A. melody
   B. echo
   C. beat
   D. lyric

9. The French rhythm name for a crotchet is (1 mark)
   A. sh
   B. taa
   C. te-te
   D. ta-te

10. Dictation in music means (1 mark)
   A. drawing a picture
   B. copying a friend's book
   C. singing louder
   D. writing down a pattern you hear

11. The sol-fa syllable r is pronounced (1 mark)
   A. ree
   B. rah
   C. ray
   D. roh

12. Why do we knead clay before using it? (1 mark)
   A. To make it dry
   B. To make it black
   C. To make it hard
   D. To make it smooth and remove air

13. What happens on the command set? (1 mark)
   A. The runners sit
   B. The runners raise their hips slightly and stay still
   C. The runners run
   D. The race ends

14. On the Kenyan flag, red stands for (1 mark)
   A. the blood shed in the struggle for freedom
   B. the land
   C. the sky
   D. peace

15. A side roll is also called a (1 mark)
   A. crab roll
   B. log roll
   C. star roll
   D. frog roll

16. In this lesson's sequence, what comes after the crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. Netball pass
   B. Sprint start
   C. Side roll immediately
   D. Lower the hips to the mat

17. The message of a song is (1 mark)
   A. the colour of the stage
   B. the main idea the singers want us to hear
   C. the name of the drum
   D. the number of singers

18. A folk song is (1 mark)
   A. a traditional song belonging to a community
   B. a song without a message
   C. a computer song
   D. a song only for cities

19. The screen of a camera (1 mark)
   A. is the battery
   B. shows what you will photograph and photos you have taken
   C. makes sound
   D. is the strap

20. Where must you never take photographs? (1 mark)
   A. In the playground with permission
   B. In private places such as toilets
   C. In the classroom with permission
   D. At the school gate

21. When you blow into the recorder, the sound is made by (1 mark)
   A. a drum skin
   B. air vibrating inside it
   C. the wood being struck
   D. a string

22. How many finger holes are on the front of the descant recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Seven
   B. Twelve
   C. Five
   D. Three

23. The bottom part of the recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. foot joint
   B. head joint
   C. beak
   D. thumb hole

24. Outside the pool, in a river or the sea, you should (1 mark)
   A. swim alone
   B. only go in with a trusted adult who can swim
   C. go in at night
   D. dive from rocks

25. Which Kiswahili word means elephant? (1 mark)
   A. twiga
   B. nyoka
   C. kuku
   D. tembo

26. How should you care for displayed works? (1 mark)
   A. Tear the corners
   B. Touch to feel the paint
   C. Do not touch or write on them
   D. Leave them in the rain

27. Which is a component of a folk song? (1 mark)
   A. Weight
   B. Price
   C. Distance
   D. Community of origin

28. Which is an example of appropriate behaviour when viewing a display? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing at others
   B. Being quiet and respectful
   C. Running
   D. Touching wet paint

29. On which occasion may the national anthem be sung? (1 mark)
   A. Never
   B. A private joke
   C. Only at night
   D. Madaraka Day celebrations

30. Which is a focus when analysing a team sport performance? (1 mark)
   A. The colour of shoes only
   B. Teamwork and safety
   C. The price of the ball
   D. The weather only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. State how many finger holes a descant recorder has in front and where the thumb hole is. (2 marks)

32. Give three qualities of a neat montage. (3 marks)

33. State four rules of netball. (4 marks)

34. State four safety rules for the swimming pool. (4 marks)

35. Explain how to make a slab and a coil from clay. (3 marks)

36. Explain why a pair of quavers is the same length as one crotchet. (3 marks)

37. State four things to think about when analysing an art work. (4 marks)

38. Describe how you would improvise a rhythm to accompany a song. (4 marks)

39. Name the three joints of a descant recorder and state where the mouthpiece is. (3 marks)

40. Describe how to learn the East African Community anthem for performance. (4 marks)

41. Describe how to play a mini-netball game safely and fairly from warm-up to the end. (5 marks)

42. How do you select the best photographs? (3 marks)

43. Describe the steps for painting a picture of one object that shows colour value. (5 marks)

44. State three occasions when the Kenya National Anthem is sung. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Fresh air can make hot charcoal catch fire
   Air can make hot charcoal burn, so we wait until it is fully cool.

2. D — The stick or hand that strikes it
   The beater is what hits the drumhead.

3. A — higher
   A tighter skin vibrates faster and gives a higher sound.

4. B — GS and GA
   Only the Goal Shooter and the Goal Attack may score.

5. C — White
   White makes a tint, a lighter tone.

6. B — green
   Yellow and blue give green.

7. A — yellow and blue
   Green sits between the two primary colours that make it.

8. C — beat
   The beat is the steady pulse we tap or clap along to.

9. B — taa
   Taa is the name for one long sound in one beat.

10. D — writing down a pattern you hear
   In dictation, the teacher plays or claps and you write it.

11. C — ray
   The syllable r is ray.

12. D — To make it smooth and remove air
   Kneading makes clay smooth and easy to shape.

13. B — The runners raise their hips slightly and stay still
   On set, runners lift the hips and hold still.

14. A — the blood shed in the struggle for freedom
   Red stands for the blood shed for freedom.

15. B — log roll
   Keeping the body straight like a log gives it the name log roll.

16. D — Lower the hips to the mat
   You lower the hips, lie straight, then roll.

17. B — the main idea the singers want us to hear
   Message is the main idea.

18. A — a traditional song belonging to a community
   Folk songs are passed on by singing.

19. B — shows what you will photograph and photos you have taken
   The screen displays the view and the saved pictures.

20. B — In private places such as toilets
   Privacy must be respected.

21. B — air vibrating inside it
   The air inside vibrates.

22. A — Seven
   There are seven on the front and one thumb hole at the back.

23. A — foot joint
   The foot joint ends in the bell.

24. B — only go in with a trusted adult who can swim
   Open water is more dangerous.

25. D — tembo
   Tembo is an elephant.

26. C — Do not touch or write on them
   Care keeps them safe.

27. D — Community of origin
   Components include community, type, message, participants and instruments.

28. B — Being quiet and respectful
   Respect for others' work is important.

29. D — Madaraka Day celebrations
   It is sung on national days and at official events.

30. B — Teamwork and safety
   Teamwork and safety matter.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Seven finger holes in front and the thumb hole is at the back.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clean cut edges, no glue marks, well-overlapped pieces, firmly stuck and a clear title. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: No running with the ball; pass or shoot within three seconds; no contact; defenders stand 0.9 metres away; start with a centre pass. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Swim only when watched; never swim alone; walk on the pool side; no pushing; no diving in shallow water; follow the whistle. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Flatten the clay with a rolling pin until even for a slab. Roll a small piece between palms for a coil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the slab, 1 mark for the coil, 1 mark for even thickness.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: A quaver is half a beat. Half plus half makes one whole beat. A crotchet is one beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Aesthetic, skills, message and behaviour. Feedback is also accepted.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sing the song and find the beat by tapping. Play the beat on an instrument. Change to a pattern, such as two quick sounds and a long sound. Repeat it and change it at the end of a verse.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step, up to 4.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Head joint, middle joint and foot joint. The mouthpiece is on the head joint.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the joints, 1 mark for order or naming all, 1 mark for the mouthpiece.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to it several times, read and discuss the words, clap the rhythm, sing line by line and then sing the whole song together in unison while standing straight and respectful.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Warm up with jogging and stretching. Choose fair teams and positions. Check the ground and the ball. Move into space, pass early and play your position. Follow the rules, obey the umpire and thank the other team.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each stage: warm-up, fair teams, checking, playing skills, fair ending.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Check for good light, a clear subject, sharpness and no distractions, and delete the poor ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose an object and place it near a window. Draw the outline lightly. Mix the main colour and paint the object. Add a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side. Blend the edges and add a shadow, then let it dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five clear steps.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: School assembly, Madaraka Day, Mashujaa Day, Jamhuri Day, sports events and other official ceremonies. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
